winner_analysis.why_it_won: Parent humor and a recognizable scene with a teenager create a “that's my life too” feeling. The product is framed as the fix for a small family conflict, not just socks.
winner_analysis.keep_unchanged: Everything after second 3: the floor covered in socks, the SockLock box, the magnet-in-the-cuff explanation, pairs after the wash, the line “He still doesn't fold them. But they're pairs.” and the quiz offer.

variants.hook_visual: Mom stands in the bedroom doorway holding two different socks like evidence; title card “Exhibit A”.
variants.first_line: Exhibit A: the socks my son calls a pair.
variants.why: The courtroom metaphor is funny and recognizable, and keeps the tone of the original.

variants.hook_visual: Close-up: a laundry hamper overflowing with mismatched socks, mom's hand in frame.
variants.first_line: Raising a teenager means sorting socks. Forever.
variants.why: The parent's pain, endless sorting, without blaming the kid.

variants.hook_visual: Selfie shot: mom whispers into the camera next to her son's closed door.
variants.first_line: He doesn't know I'm filming his sock situation.
variants.why: Secret filming adds intrigue and humor in a UGC sketch format.

variants.hook_visual: Kinetic text over a shot of the bedroom door, the door slowly opens.
variants.first_line: I finally found where my son's socks disappear to.
variants.why: A promise to reveal a mystery, and the cut to the floor in the body delivers the answer.

variants.hook_visual: Mom sorts socks on the bed and suddenly tosses them over her shoulder.
variants.first_line: I stopped matching my son's socks. Best decision ever.
variants.why: An unexpected “I stopped” intrigues, and the body explains why it became possible.

variants.hook_visual: The son lazily tosses two SockLock socks into the hamper, and they click together mid-air (slow motion, simple motion graphics).
variants.first_line: Even a teenager can't separate these.
variants.why: Shows the product through the original's hero; “teen-proof” is a short, clear promise.

variants.hook_visual: A family group chat mockup on a phone screen: mom writes “Whose sock is this??”, three replies say “not mine”.
variants.first_line: Every week in our family group chat:
variants.why: A chat mockup is a native format that's easy to build in motion, with recognizable family humor.

variants.hook_visual: Morning: the son runs to the school bus in two different socks, freeze frame on his feet with a caption.
variants.first_line: My son just left for school in two different socks. Again.
variants.why: A concrete morning scene; repeating “Again” amplifies the pain and leads to the fix.

warnings: H07 is a family chat mockup, a staged scene. Don't present it as a real customer review.
H06 “Teen-proof socks” is a mild exaggeration. Don't back it up with numbers or guarantees.
